subject: Next steps & procurement path — Aurelia executive recap and ops unblock
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: executive priorities, procurement path, and ops unblock (Aurelia)

Daniel — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and can move procurement/ops in parallel.

Key business outcomes you emphasized:
- Reduce claims processing latency by 60% and shrink manual review by the end of Q4.
- Protect PHI and avoid any vendor-facing access to raw logs; you highlighted on-prem or VPC options for regulated pipelines.
- Predictable unit cost for inference to justify pilot-to-production ROI.

Primary risks / gating items we captured on the call:
1) Security evidence: SOC 2 + logging + KMS integration — procurement needs artifacts.
2) Deployment model: you prefer VPC-first, but need a validation window for latency and autoscaling behavior.
3) Contract path: legal wants a limited liability carveout and an SLA addendum — procurement will scope the exact uptime/credits.

Immediate next steps we proposed and owners:
- I will send the implementation checklist and a proposed SLA sideletter for your legal review (action: Kimberly) — attached.
- Ben to assemble a tailored performance runbook for your expected payload (action: Ben).
- Please introduce your procurement lead; we’ll share a DocuSign-friendly redline and checklist to get a P.O. or MSA underway (action: Aurelia).

Suggested timeline:
- Week 1: procurement intro + evidence handoff
- Week 2: performance validation in VPC staging (2-week window)
- Week 4: pilot kickoff pending legal/commercial sign-off

Attachments included: implementation checklist (xlsx), draft SLA sideletter (pdf).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Ben’s runbook and a short one-pager for your CFO.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0189

--
Attachment: redwood-implementation-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)
Attachment: redwood-sla-sideletter.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Procurement: looping in Sara Patel (cc'd) — she owns vendor onboarding and contract redlines.
- Security: SOC 2 report and KMS integration diagram will be necessary for our InfoSec review. Can you provide the diagrams and an account of where logs are stored/retained?
- Timeline: we can target staging validation the week of July 27, but legal will need the SLA sideletter by next Wednesday to start redlines.

Also, our CFO asked about an estimated monthly run rate for a 100k token/day pilot (ballpark numbers sufficient for budgeting). If you can include a short estimate in the one-pager, that would help move the commercial conversation.

Appreciate it — Daniel

Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: performance runbook & validation plan for Aurelia (draft)

Kimberly / Lauren — drafting a targeted runbook for the 100k token/day pilot. High-level plan:
- Day 0–3: ingest sample traffic, validate sequence lengths and KV cache hit rates.
- Day 4–7: run latency profile in VPC staging across 95/99 percentiles; capture token-level cost breakdown.
- Day 8–14: validate autoscaling policy under burst traffic patterns described by Aurelia.

Open questions for the call with Aurelia's engineering team:
- Will they allow a 24-hour window to ship anonymized samples to our staging environment, or do we need to run entirely on their side?
- Any FHIR-specific transformations we should account for?

I pulled the baseline latency numbers for the recommended model and attached a short CSV. I’ll insert a short cost estimate for the CFO one-pager and a recommended conservative burst policy.

Ben

ben.carter@redwood.ai

- Proposed kickoff: Aug 3 (engineering ramp + onboarding) contingent on P.O. or signed MSA by 7/30.
